questions.statement: Which sentence uses the causative correctly?

options.text: She had her hair cut at the salon.
options.feedback: 'Have something done' expresses that someone else performs the action.

options.text: She had cut her hair at the salon.
options.feedback: 'Had cut' would mean she performed the action herself in the past.

options.text: She has cut her hair at the salon.
options.feedback: That says she cut it herself, without causative meaning.

options.text: She is hair cut at the salon.
options.feedback: 'Is' plus participle does not express the causative structure.

questions.explanation:
La estructura causative causative indica que una persona Provoca una accion realize otra persona.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'They are building a new library; the contractor ____ it for the city council.'

options.text: has built
options.feedback: 'Is building' with 'has built' means the contractor performs the building.

options.text: is building
options.feedback: That would mean the city council itself is doing the work.

options.text: builds
options.feedback: A bare verb gives no causative meaning.

options.text: built
options.feedback: The past simple refers to a completed past action, not to the ongoing one.

questions.explanation:
La forma causative exige 'have/get' mas objeto mas participio, y el presente coincide con la accion en curso.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does 'I got my car repaired' mean?

options.text: The speaker repaired the car personally
options.feedback: That would be 'I repaired my car'.

options.text: The car was stolen
options.feedback: Nothing in the sentence refers to theft.

options.text: The speaker bought a new car
options.feedback: 'Repaired' means fixed, not replaced.

options.text: The speaker had someone else repair the car
options.feedback: 'Got it repaired' means the repair was done by another person.

questions.explanation:
'Get' mas objeto mas participio expresa que el hablante llevo el coche a un taller sin ejecutarlo el mismo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses 'have' plus participle correctly?

options.text: I have my windows cleaned every month.
options.feedback: The cleaning is performed by another person on a regular basis.

options.text: I have clean my windows every month.
options.feedback: The second verb must be the participle 'cleaned', not the base form.

options.text: I am clean my windows every month.
options.feedback: 'Am' cannot be followed by a bare verb in this structure.

options.text: I cleaning my windows every month.
options.feedback: A gerund alone cannot function as the causative verb group.

questions.explanation:
En la estructura causative el 'have' es el auxiliar y el participio expresa la accion Encargada.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'I had cut my hair very short.' What does it mean?

options.text: A hairdresser cut the speaker's hair
options.feedback: That requires the causative 'had it cut'.

options.text: The speaker cut the speaker's own hair
options.feedback: 'Had cut' without a following participle is the simple past perfect of 'cut'.

options.text: The speaker will cut the hair tomorrow
options.feedback: Nothing in the sentence refers to the future.

options.text: The hair was cut by the speaker last week
options.feedback: The sentence does not specify last week; it only uses the past perfect.

questions.explanation:
Sin el participio, 'had cut' significa que el hablante se corto el pelo el mismo, no que se lo cortaron.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the causative question: 'Where did you ____ your phone repaired?'

options.text: did get
options.feedback: Repeating 'did' makes the sentence ungrammatical.

options.text: getting
options.feedback: A gerund cannot open a past question with 'did'.

options.text: be
options.feedback: 'Be' plus participle forms the passive voice, not the causative question.

options.text: get
options.feedback: 'Did you get it repaired?' is a standard causative question.

questions.explanation:
En pasado el causative usa 'did' mas objeto mas 'have' mas participio, o directamente 'get' mas participio.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence expresses the causative in the future?

options.text: I will paint the kitchen next month.
options.feedback: That says the speaker will do the painting personally.

options.text: I will have the kitchen painted next month.
options.feedback: 'Will have' plus participle expresses a future causative arrangement.

options.text: I have the kitchen painted next month.
options.feedback: The simple present would place the arrangement in a habitual sense, not clearly in the future.

options.text: I am painting the kitchen next month.
options.feedback: The present continuous plus 'next month' is awkward; the causative frame is required.

questions.explanation:
Para expresar el causative en el futuro se usa 'will have' mas objeto mas participio.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the difference between 'have' and 'get' in the causative?

options.text: 'Get' expresses the speaker doing the action
options.feedback: Both forms place the action in someone else's hands.

options.text: 'Have' is only used in questions
options.feedback: The causative with 'have' appears mainly in statements.

options.text: They are completely unrelated in meaning
options.feedback: They are variants of the same causative structure.

options.text: 'Have' is standard; 'get' is a common informal alternative
options.feedback: Both express that another person performs the action.

questions.explanation:
'Have something done' es la forma estandar; 'get something done' es mas coloquial y significa lo mismo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the causative passive.

options.text: They had repair the roof before the rains.
options.feedback: The second verb must be a participle, not the base form 'repair'.

options.text: They had the roof repair before the rains.
options.feedback: The bare 'repair' lacks the passive form 'repaired'.

options.text: They had the roof repaired before the rains.
options.feedback: 'Roof repaired' is the passive participle of the action done to the roof.

options.text: They got the roof to repair before the rains.
options.feedback: 'Get' plus infinitive does not express the causative here.

questions.explanation:
En el causative pasivo el 'have/get' va seguido de un participio pasivo que describe la accion sobre un objeto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text: 'After the storm, the family had the roof repaired and the walls repainted.' What is the meaning?

options.text: The family repaired and repainted everything themselves
options.feedback: That would require the simple past 'repaired' without 'had'.

options.text: The family built a new house
options.feedback: The text mentions repairs, not a new construction.

options.text: The family moved to another house
options.feedback: No change of residence is mentioned in the text.

options.text: Other people repaired the roof and repainted the walls
options.feedback: The causative 'had done' assigns the work to hired professionals.

questions.explanation:
Ambas acciones fueron realizadas por otras personas hired, no por la familia misma. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is NOT a causative construction?

options.text: They had a good time at the party.
options.feedback: 'Have a good time' is an idiom meaning 'enjoy yourself', not a causative.

options.text: They had the car washed.
options.feedback: 'Had the car washed' is a causative with a passive participle.

options.text: He had his photograph taken.
options.feedback: 'Had his photograph taken' is a causative structure.

options.text: We had the walls painted.
options.feedback: 'Had the walls painted' is a causative structure.

questions.explanation:
La frase 'have a good time' es una expresion idiomatica y no una estructura causative.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The office ____ its carpets cleaned every week.'
questions.context: Causative en contexto de servicios, Guayaquil.

options.text: have
options.feedback: 'Have' does not agree with the singular subject 'the office'.

options.text: is
options.feedback: 'Is' plus 'cleaning' would mean the office cleans the carpets itself.

options.text: has
options.feedback: 'Has' agrees with the singular subject and fits the habitual causative.

options.text: are
options.feedback: 'Are' does not agree with the singular subject 'the office'.

questions.explanation:
El sujeto 'the office' encarga el trabajo y el auxiliar 'has' concuerda con el presente habitual.

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly uses the causative with 'get' in the past?

options.text: She got her computer fixed at the shop.
options.feedback: 'Got it fixed' is a standard past causative with 'get'.

options.text: She got fix her computer at the shop.
options.feedback: After 'got' the verb must be the participle 'fixed'.

options.text: She gets fix her computer at the shop.
options.feedback: The base form after the participle position is wrong here.

options.text: She is get her computer fixed at the shop.
options.feedback: 'Is' cannot be combined with 'get' in the causative.

questions.explanation:
En pasado, 'get' mas objeto mas participio aparece con 'did' o directamente en la oracion afirmativa.

questions.statement: Look at the question: 'Did you have your car serviced before the trip?' How should it be answered?

options.text: Yes, I serviced it on Monday.
options.feedback: That says the speaker did the work, which loses the causative meaning.

options.text: Yes, I am servicing it on Monday.
options.feedback: The present continuous does not answer a past question.

options.text: Yes, I had it serviced on Monday.
options.feedback: 'Had it serviced' keeps the causative frame and the past time.

options.text: Yes, it was serviced by me.
options.feedback: The passive here suggests the speaker did it, contradicting the causative question.

questions.explanation:
Una respuesta coherente mantiene el pasado y aclara si el trabajo lo hizo alguien mas.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which statement about the causative is correct?

options.text: It describes an action performed by the subject itself
options.feedback: That is the plain active voice, not the causative.

options.text: It describes making someone else perform an action
options.feedback: That is precisely the meaning of the causative structure.

options.text: It describes an action that did not happen
options.feedback: A hypothetical is expressed with conditionals, not with the causative.

options.text: It is used only with animate subjects
options.feedback: Inanimate subjects such as 'the office' appear frequently in causative sentences.

questions.explanation:
El causativehift describe una accion en la que el sujeto Provoca que otro la realice.

questions.statement: Choose the correct passive participle: 'She had her dress ____ before the party.'

options.text: maked
options.feedback: 'Maked' is not an English participle.

options.text: made
options.feedback: 'Made' is the correct past participle of 'make' for this passive construction.

options.text: make
options.feedback: 'Make' is the base form and does not work after the causative auxiliary.

options.text: making
options.feedback: 'Making' is the gerund and does not fit this position.

questions.explanation:
El participio pasivo de 'make' para una prenda es 'made', y la frase completa expresa el causative.

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the causative correctly with a time expression?

options.text: We have the generator installed last semester.
options.feedback: The present perfect is incompatible with the closed time 'last semester'.

options.text: We had install the generator last semester.
options.feedback: After 'had' the verb must be the participle 'installed'.

options.text: We are having install the generator last semester.
options.feedback: The present continuous cannot be combined with a closed past time.

options.text: We had the generator installed last semester.
options.feedback: 'Had installed' with a closed past time is a correct causative.

questions.explanation:
El causative en pasado con un tiempo cerrado se enuncia con 'had' mas participio, sin auxiliares adicionales.

questions.statement: Read the sentence: 'The hotel had the rooms renovated in 2018.' What does 'renovated' express?

options.text: The action performed by the guests
options.feedback: The guests are not the ones who renovate; the causative assigns it to others.

options.text: The action performed to the rooms by someone else
options.feedback: The passive participle marks the action done to the object.

options.text: A future intention of the hotel
options.feedback: The time 'in 2018' is past, not future.

options.text: A refusal to renovate
options.feedback: The sentence states the renovation took place.

questions.explanation:
'Renovated' es el participio pasivo que describe la accion ejecutada sobre las habitaciones.

questions.statement: Which option correctly completes: 'They are getting the generator ____ before the storm arrives.'

options.text: to check
options.feedback: 'To check' would be an infinitive, not the required participle.

options.text: check
options.feedback: The bare base form does not fit the causative structure.

options.text: checked
options.feedback: 'Getting it checked' presents the check as an action in progress.

options.text: for checking
options.feedback: The preposition is not part of this structure.

questions.explanation:
En presente continuo el causative usa 'getting' mas objeto mas participio para una accion que se esta Realizando.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does the causative allow the speaker to emphasise?

options.text: The identity of the worker
options.feedback: The worker is usually anonymous in the causative structure.

options.text: The place where the action takes place
options.feedback: Location is expressed by prepositional phrases, not by the causative.

options.text: The result obtained, rather than the person who performs the action
options.feedback: The causative foregrounds the result of having something done.

options.text: The exact price of the service
options.feedback: Cost would appear in a separate sentence about payment.

questions.explanation:
El causative destaca el resultado y la accion del objeto, mas que la persona que la ejecuta.
